title: Article III §§ 1–2 — federal judicial power
summary: Subject-matter jurisdiction is a court’s authority to decide a category of dispute. Federal courts require an applicable grant of authority within the limits allowed by the Constitution.

sections.Role in the course: Subject-matter jurisdiction is a court’s authority to decide a category of dispute. Federal courts require an applicable grant of authority within the limits allowed by the Constitution.
sections.What to examine: Identify the statute authorizing the federal claim or action. The course emphasizes diversity, federal questions, supplemental jurisdiction, and removal. State the jurisdictional facts, distinguish them from facts proving liability, and check any statutory restrictions.
